 ‘I tried my best, but could not save them’: Staffer who jumped into Bengaluru 5-star hotel pool to rescue two foreigners stable, but traumatised 
 Trending IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das ‘I tried my best, but could not save them’: Staffer who jumped into Bengaluru 5-star hotel pool to rescue two foreigners stable, but traumatised 
 Jahnavi T R / TNN / Updated: Nov 01, 2026, 07:43 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print (AI-IMAGE) A heartbreaking occurrence transpired at the Conrad Hotel's swimming pool, claiming the lives of two foreign nationals BENGALURU: “I could not save the two people in the pool. I tried my best.” Even as he lay in a hospital bed on Saturday, recovering from injuries sustained while trying to rescue two foreign nationals from a swimming pool, these were the words of Rahul Tiwari , a pool attendant at the Conrad Hotel. Having jumped into the pool Friday evening in an attempt to save the two men, Tiwari was struggling to come to terms with the fact that, despite his best efforts, he could not save their lives. It had begun as an otherwise routine evening at the hotel. As the afternoon sun gave way to dusk, Alexander Maximilian Theiss, Juraj Horvat and US national Mathews Desantis decided to take a dip in the swimming pool. However, what began as a leisurely swim soon turned into a tragedy. According to sources, at around 5.11 pm, Desantis felt an electric current in the water while swimming. He managed to make his way back to safety and alerted Tiwari. Without a moment’s hesitation, the pool attendant jumped into the water in an attempt to rescue Theiss and Horvat. However, by then, it was too late. All four men were rushed to Manipal Hospital on Old Airport Road, where they arrived at around 5.45 pm. According to Dr Mabel Vasnaik, head of the department of emergency medicine at Manipal Hospitals, Theiss was brought dead. Doctors attempted to resuscitate Horvat but were unsuccessful, and he was subsequently declared dead. “The cause of death was electrocution,” Dr Vasnaik said. The two survivors, meanwhile, were assessed for their injuries. “The US national complained of a headache Friday and was in shock. However, as of Saturday, he was stable and was likely to be discharged by the evening. The pool attendant, who jumped into the water to save them, is also stable but reported some pain Saturday. We will conduct X-rays to rule out any fractures and discharge him today as well,” she told TOI . While Tiwari was physically stable, the incident appeared to have taken a considerable emotional toll on him. A source said he was inconsolable and reluctant to speak to anyone. “He is crying a lot and does not want to speak to anyone. He feels guilty that he could not save the two men. He is also in shock,” the source said, adding, “He instinctively jumped into the pool. That was a brave thing to do.” When TOI visited the hospital, Tiwari was accompanied by an attendant. A fellow patient in the room said they did not know much about him, adding that he had barely spoken since Friday. Tiwari declined to speak when approached by TOI . A nurse, however, said he was doing well and recovering gradually. C onrad management says it will cooperate with investigators In a statement issued Saturday, Conrad Bengaluru spokesperson said, “We are saddened by the tragic incident which occurred at Conrad Bengaluru yesterday, leading to the subsequent passing away of two guests. We offer our deepest condolences to all those impacted. The cause of the incident has not yet been established and remains subject to a comprehensive investigation by local authorities. We are offering our full support to their investigation. ” Lufthansa seeks alternative hotel for crew While a section of the German media described Alexander Theiss as a flight captain, Lufthansa said he was a member of the crew that had arrived in Bengaluru and that the deaths occurred during their layover. While the other crew members were resting, Theiss had stepped out to use the swimming pool. A German publication reported that the surviving crew members were deeply shaken by the incident and were receiving psychological support. It also reported that Lufthansa crew members had sought a change of hotel accommodation in Bengaluru following the tragedy. (With inputs from Vindhya Pabolu)
